class.name: TweensGdHandle
class.brief_description: A playback handle for one tween, independent of its definition.
class.description: Returned by [code]Tweens.play[/code] or [method TweensGdScheduler.add]. Await [member end] before starting the next step; use [method pause], [method resume], and [method cancel] to control playback. Controls use Godot's main thread. C# equivalent: [code]TweenInstance[/code]. C# faults throw from [code]End[/code]; GDScript returns [code]Tweens.Reason.FAILED[/code] and stores the message in [member error]. [codeblock] var handle := Tweens.play(sprite, Tweens.position_2d(Vector2(400, 180), 0.6)) if await handle.end != Tweens.Reason.COMPLETED: return await Tweens.play(sprite, Tweens.modulate_alpha(0.0, 0.3)).end [/codeblock]

method.name: cancel
method.description: Stops active playback with [code]Tweens.Reason.CANCELLED[/code]. Ended playback is unchanged.

method.name: pause
method.description: Explicitly pauses playback. Scene and owner pause modes apply separately.

method.name: rejected
method.description: Creates an already-ended result with [code]Tweens.Reason.FAILED[/code] and [param message] in [member error].

method.name: resume
method.description: Clears the explicit pause. Scene and owner pause modes still apply.

method.name: wait
method.description: Waits for playback to end. [param cancellation] cancels this wait, leaving playback running. Await the returned value; cancellation returns [code]Tweens.Reason.WAIT_CANCELLED[/code]. Without a token this is equivalent to [member end]. C# handle equivalent: [code]AwaitDecommissionAsync(token)[/code], which throws on wait cancellation.

members.member: Why playback ended, or -1 while running. Uses [code]Tweens.Reason[/code]; C# uses null while running.

Shared completion. Await this value: it is a Signal while running and the integer completion reason after settlement, so late awaits are safe. Cancellation returns a reason; failure returns [code]Tweens.Reason.FAILED[/code] with [member error]. Independent playback created by callbacks or awaits starts on the next eligible update with no inherited time. Use [TweensGdChain] for linked timing.
Failure message, or an empty string. C# uses an Exception or null.
Explicit playback pause. Owner and scene pause modes apply separately.
True once playback and all terminal callbacks finished. Late awaits return immediately.
True once playback completed, was cancelled, or faulted. Terminal callbacks may still be running.
Uneased progress in [code][0, 1][/code]. Decreases on the ping-pong return leg.
Current timeline state from [code]Tweens.State[/code]. Explicit pausing does not change it.
The target animated by this playback, or null if it has been freed.
Last sampled value, including easing and delay fill.

signal.name: ended
signal.description: Emitted once after playback settles, with its completion reason. Prefer awaiting [member end], which also handles already-ended playback.
